title: Uniqueness of Simultaneity
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0011050v1 (submitted 2000-11-14, report no. ZU-TH 25/00); published as Brit. J. Phil. Sci. 52(4):651-670 (2001), DOI 10.1093/bjps/52.4.651 (DOI cross-checked via Semantic Scholar record; journal ref stated on arXiv landing page)
section_locator: arXiv HTML v1: Req.1/Req.2 (absolute vs relative simultaneity, soundness criterion 'classes meet any physically realizable trajectory in at most one point'); Thm 1 (existence criterion: non-maximal stabilizers); Thm 2-3 (Galilei case: classes are planes or unions mod lambda; standard Galilean simultaneity unique); Thm 4 (no nontrivial ILor-invariant equivalence relation, hence no absolute simultaneity in Lorentzian case); Thm 5 (ILor_X classification for X = inertial frame: orthogonal hyperplanes, unions mod lambda, the line, unions of lattice points); Thm 6 (Einstein simultaneity unique relative to an inertial frame under Req.2); Thm 7 + Appendix (re-proof of Malament's uniqueness using Alexandrov's characterization of causal automorphisms); Sec. 5 (critique of Sarkar-Stachel proof gap: G-invariant partitions need not have G-invariant classes; onion/shell counterexamples when dilations are dropped)
assumptions: Flat spacetime R^4; simultaneity = equivalence relation; automorphism group Aut = inhomogeneous Galilei or inhomogeneous Lorentz group (proper orthochronous, no reflections, no dilations), motivated by affine structure + relativity principle + boost equivariance; X = single observer worldline or foliation by parallel timelike lines (inertial frame); invariance of the partition under the stabilizer Aut_X; soundness: classes meet physically realizable (timelike) trajectories at most once.
conclusion: Paper's claims: with Aut=ILor there is no nontrivial invariant equivalence relation at all (no absolute simultaneity); relative to an inertial frame with the soundness condition, Einstein simultaneity is unique; Malament's theorem is re-derived for the single-worldline case with causal automorphisms (which include dilations and time reflections). Section 5 exhibits additional invariant equivalence relations (concentric-shell 'onion' partitions, tilted half-cones) that appear once dilations or time reflections are dropped from the invariance group, and identifies the exact step where Sarkar-Stachel's uniqueness proof fails.
proof_status: Full text read including appendix proof of Thm 7; statements and proof strategy inspected, not independently reproduced.
open_questions: Giulini uses the physical-symmetry group rather than causal automorphisms; the two choices give different classifications, and which group is 'correct' depends on prior commitments about what counts as given structure (his Sec. 1 fn 2 and Sec. 5). Mamone-Capria 2012 corrects two of Giulini's classification theorems (everywhere-dense subgroups missed); the corrected statements are in axrel-mamone-capria-2012.
relevance: Systematic group-theoretic classification of simultaneity relations; pins down exactly which invariance-group choices give uniqueness. Direct predecessor for any assumption-dependency graph of simultaneity.
limits: Flat spacetime only; equivalence-relation assumption not itself justified against conventionalist 'causal theory of simultaneity' (author notes this is contestable). No ontological conclusion is drawn or licensed.

title: Simultaneity as an Invariant Equivalence Relation
version: arXiv:1202.6578v3 (2012-07-26); published as Found. Phys. 42:1365-1383 (2012), DOI 10.1007/s10701-012-9674-4 (both checked on arXiv landing page and Semantic Scholar record)
section_locator: arXiv HTML v3: Thm 2.5 (G-invariant equivalences <-> G0-invariant additive subgroups); Thm 3.3 (Newton-invariant classes); Thm 3.6 (Galilei-invariant classes, correcting Giulini's Thm 2: everywhere-dense subgroup case); Prop 3.8 + Cor 3.9 (no nontrivial orthochronous-Poincare-invariant equivalences); Prop 3.10 (join of two non-proportional standard synchronies is universal; meet of four is identity); Thm 3.15 (two-way light isotropy + preservation of causal statements forces standard synchrony up to scale); Thm 3.16 (Alexandrov restated); Thm 3.17 (frame-isotropy classification, correcting Giulini's Thm 5; part B: standard synchrony unique under conformal frame group if classes are not worldlines); Cor 3.18 (3-dimensional or connected classes force standard synchrony); Thm 3.19 (unified restatement+proof of Malament 1977 Prop 2 and Sarkar-Stachel half-cone alternative); Prop 4.1 (Hogarth 2005 proposition re-proved); Sec. 4 discussion
assumptions: R^4 with Newton, Galilei, or Poincare group actions; simultaneity construed as G-invariant equivalence relation, classified via invariant additive subgroups; causality condition: causally connectible events cannot be simultaneous; in Thm 3.19 the single worldline l with normalized future vector u, isotropy subgroups G_N (rotations+dilations+translations along l, no time inversion) vs G_M (adding time inversion), nontotal equivalence with some class of a point of l not contained in l.
conclusion: Paper's claims: complete classification of Newton/Galilei/Poincare-invariant equivalence relations (with corrections to Giulini); Malament's uniqueness holds exactly when time-inversion invariance (within the causal-automorphism group with dilations) is required; without it, translated half-cones C_c^+ or C_c^- of arbitrary opening appear; Hogarth's no-dilation variant also yields uniqueness but still assumes time inversion; two-way light isotropy plus preservation of causality already forces standard synchrony (Thm 3.15); overall, the invariant-equivalence interpretation does not settle the conventionality debate because adherents of the causal theory of simultaneity reject the equivalence-relation requirement itself and any appeal to the Poincare group's one-way isotropy.
proof_status: Full text read; proofs inspected (they are short and group-theoretic), not independently reproduced.
open_questions: Whether a classification without the equivalence-relation assumption (arbitrary simultaneity-like relations) exists in this line; author defers the block-universe discussion to future work (Sec. 3.3 fn 7).
relevance: The most complete single-source ablation study of the invariance parameters (group choice, time inversion, dilations, frame vs worldline, topological class conditions) with explicit corrections of predecessors.
limits: Author's own position (Mamone-Capria 2001) that standard synchrony deserves privilege is asserted, not derived here. No curved spacetime; no ontology conclusion; explicit statement that this interpretation does not cut into the conventionality debate.

title: Conventionality of Simultaneity: Malament's Result Revisited
version: Foundations of Physics Letters 18:491-497 (2005); DOI 10.1007/s10702-005-7539-1 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-19; bibliographic data also matches reference [7] of arXiv:1202.6578v3)
section_locator: Not accessed; proposition known through Mamone-Capria 2012, Prop 4.1, which restates and proves it
assumptions: Per Mamone-Capria's restatement: equivalence relation on R^4 whose classes each meet the worldline l in exactly one point; invariance under the isotropy subgroup G_M of l in the Poincare-plus-dilations group with time inversion but without further dilation freedom (G_M rather than G^_M).
conclusion: As restated and proved by Mamone-Capria (Prop 4.1): the relation must be standard synchrony R_u. The original paper text has not been inspected; the attribution of this proposition to Hogarth rests on Mamone-Capria's reference.
proof_status: Not independently checked against the original; the re-proof in Mamone-Capria 2012 was read.
open_questions: Verify Hogarth's own formulation and whether he also treats the no-time-inversion case.
relevance: Shows a variant soundness condition (unique representative on the worldline) recovering uniqueness without dilations.
limits: Abstract-level record: paywalled/not located publicly; do not cite the proposition without the Mamone-Capria restatement caveat.

title: David Malament and the Conventionality of Simultaneity: A Reply
version: Foundations of Physics 40:1285-1297 (2010); DOI 10.1007/s10701-009-9328-3 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-19)
section_locator: Not accessed; content characterized via SEP Conventionality of Simultaneity entry (2018 revision), Sec. 3, and Mamone-Capria 2012 Sec. 4 fn 9
assumptions: Per SEP summary: treats Malament's postulate that simultaneity is an equivalence relation as a weakness; revives Janis 1983 per-observer latitude argument.
conclusion: As reported by SEP and Mamone-Capria: Malament's theorem yields a unique (but different) synchrony for each inertial observer, the same latitude as Reichenbach's epsilon, so the theorem neither supports nor undermines conventionalism more than the simplicity argument for epsilon=1/2 does. This is the paper author's claim as summarized in secondary sources; not verified against the primary text.
proof_status: Philosophical argument; not inspected in the primary.
open_questions: Read the primary reply to check whether Grunbaum also contests explicit definability (as Rynasiewicz 2001 does).
relevance: Strongest contrary position to reading Malament's theorem as an anti-conventionalist result.
limits: Abstract/secondary only; paywalled primary not accessed.

title: Causality Implies the Lorentz Group
version: J. Math. Phys. 5(4):490-493 (1964); DOI 10.1063/1.1704140 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-19, abstract read there)
section_locator: Crossref abstract only: 'Causality is represented by a partial ordering on Minkowski space, and the group of all automorphisms that preserve this partial ordering is shown to be generated by the inhomogeneous Lorentz group and dilatations.'
assumptions: Bijection of Minkowski space preserving the causal partial order (no continuity assumed).
conclusion: Author's claim (abstract): causal-automorphism group = inhomogeneous Lorentz group + dilatations (reflections allowed since the order is partial). This underwrites the automorphism groups used in Malament/Giulini/Mamone-Capria. Giulini 2001 Sec. 5 attributes the sharper statement (with time/space reflections and dilations, and the orthochronous variant) to Alexandrov 1975.
open_questions: Alexandrov (Annali di Mat. 103:229-257, 1975) is the other half of this line; not separately verified this pass.
relevance: Foundational result: the causal order alone fixes the conformal Lorentz structure, i.e., temporal order is invariant while simultaneity is not definable from it without extra structure.
limits: Abstract-level; cite via Giulini/Mamone-Capria when precision is needed.

title: Causality and Temporal Order in Special Relativity
version: Brit. J. Phil. Sci. 57:459-479 (2006); DOI 10.1093/bjps/axl019 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-19; note: an earlier internal note had guessed axl025, which is wrong)
section_locator: Not accessed; contents reconstructed from Besnard 2011 Sec. 2 (which states Ben-Yami's soundness condition and conic-relation classification) and SEP Further Discussion supplement
assumptions: Per Besnard's account: fundamental causal relation is directed ('if e1 is a cause of e2 then e2 does not precede e1'), i.e., causal ordering ⪯ instead of symmetric kappa; simultaneity relations implicitly definable from (X, ⪯) satisfying Malament's soundness condition (Ben-Yami also considers Giulini's).
conclusion: Per Besnard: the Aut_(X,⪯)-invariant equivalence relations satisfying the soundness condition are exactly the conic relations Gamma_{X,v}^{+-} with v in ]0,∞] (past/future light cones included, Sigma_X as limit); Ben-Yami then argues an observer cannot remain inertial forever, and concludes only the light-cone relations are definable relative to an event. Ben-Yami credits Spirtes 1981 as first to note the infinity of relations once time reflections are dropped. These characterizations are as reported by Besnard (full text read); the primary paper was not accessed.
proof_status: Secondary verification only (Besnard 2011 and SEP supplement agree on the content).
open_questions: Access the primary to confirm exact statement and the later-observer argument (Besnard flags that Ben-Yami misattributes explicit definability to Rynasiewicz).
relevance: Ablation result: replacing symmetric kappa by directed causal order already yields a one-parameter family; basis of the 'directed time' variants named in NOVELTY.md candidate C.
limits: Paywalled; abstract-level record with secondary-derived content, clearly marked.

title: Twin Paradox and the Logical Foundation of Relativity Theory
version: Foundations of Physics 36:681-714 (2006); DOI 10.1007/s10701-005-9041-9 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-19)
section_locator: Not directly accessed; cited as [21] in arXiv:1105.0885v1 as the source of the AccRel formulations and of the twin-paradox ablation Theorem 7.1 (AccRel ⊢ TwP; AccRel−AxDf ⊢ TwP; AccRel−Cont ⊬ TwP; even Th(R) ∪ AccRel−Cont ⊬ TwP)
assumptions: Per 1105.0885v1: FOL axiom system AccRel = SpecRel ∪ {AxCmv, AxEv-, AxSf-, AxDf} ∪ Cont; Cont is the FOL scheme requiring suprema of definable bounded nonempty sets of quantities.
conclusion: Per the citing paper: AccRel proves the twin paradox; differentiability (AxDf) is dispensable for it; the continuity scheme is not (independence shown by model construction, and not repairable by adding the full first-order theory of the reals). These characterizations are from the citing paper, not from the primary.
proof_status: Not inspected; the independence claims should be audited here before any use.
open_questions: Audit the AccRel−Cont countermodel and the role of non-Archimedean quantity fields; check whether later Szekely work strengthens or weakens the ablation.
relevance: Primary locus of the Budapest school's axiom-ablation method (why-questions answered by dropping axioms); needed for candidate C's FOL side.
limits: Discovery-level: metadata verified; theorem content taken from the citing survey.

title: A Theory of Time and Space
version: Cambridge University Press, 1914; the archive.org URL is an unverified locator hint and was not fetched this pass
section_locator: Cited and used in Malament 1977: Prop 1(ii) (Orth definability from kappa) is 'essentially due to Robb'; Malament's notes 2-4 state that Robb used an asymmetric 'after' relation, did not worry about first-order niceties, and gave a second-order representation theorem with axioms whose models are isomorphic to (R^4, kappa)
assumptions: Per Malament's account: causal-order axioms in a second-order language with a single two-place predicate.
conclusion: Per Malament: kappa-definability of the orthogonality/light-cone structure (hence of Minkowski geometry) originates here. This is the original causal-axiomatization of Minkowski spacetime and the ancestor of the whole definability line.
proof_status: Not inspected; content known only through Malament 1977 (read this pass) and the SEP entry.
open_questions: Compare Robb's asymmetric-relation axiom set with later symmetric-kappa versions (Latzer, Winnie per Malament's references [2],[4]); count and compare axioms if candidate C proceeds.
relevance: Oldest nearest predecessor for 'axiomatize spacetime from causal order'; candidate C must position against it.

title: Conventionality of Simultaneity (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Summer 2018 revision, with supplement)
version: First published 1998-08-31; substantive revision 2018-07-21 (stated on page); supplement 'Further Discussion of Malament's Theorem' read in the same revision
section_locator: Main entry Sec. 3 'Malament's Theorem' (statement of premises); Sec. 3 final paragraphs (Grünbaum 2010, Janis 1983 per-observer latitude, Redhead, Debs-Redhead); Sec. 4 (Mamone Capria 2012, Rynasiewicz 2012 gauge-freedom argument); supplement (Havas; Anderson-Vetharaniam-Stedman error; Spirtes 1981 Ch VI Sec F; Stein 1991 p.153n; Sarkar-Stachel; Ben-Yami; Giulini with absolute-vs-relative definitions)
assumptions: Secondary exposition; uses kappa = symmetric causal connectibility, O = observer worldline.
conclusion: States Malament's theorem premises as: S definable from kappa and O; S an equivalence relation; some p on O and q off O with S(p,q); S not universal; conclusion S = standard synchrony. Records that commentators diverge: some read it as settling non-conventionality (Torretti, Norton), Grünbaum/Janis/Redhead argue it does not (per-observer latitude = epsilon latitude); debate described as not settled. The supplement adds the technical history (time-reflection requirement, dilations, proof gap in Sarkar-Stachel).
open_questions: Compare with the archived 2001 version already recorded as found-sep-malament; the 2018 revision adds the post-2001 literature.
relevance: Authoritative secondary map of the whole debate with bibliography; used to bound what the primary results do and do not claim.
limits: Secondary; its summaries of Grünbaum 2010 and Rynasiewicz 2012 are abstract-level for this lane.

title: Being and Becoming in Modern Physics (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, October 2021 revision)
version: First published 2001-07-11; substantive revision 2021-10-06 (stated on page)
section_locator: Sec. 3 intro (light-cone regions; Rietdijk-Putnam-Penrose 'chronogeometrical fatalism' argument via Penrose's Andromeda example); Sec. 3.2 (Stein 1968/1991 approach: R as two-place 'has become/already definite' relation; transitivity, reflexivity, non-universality; answer: y in/on past light cone of x; Stein 1968 p.15 quote 'an event's present is constituted by itself alone'; Callender 2000 non-uniqueness objection; Yourgrau objection); Sec. 3.3 (Robb-Stein-Dieks point presents; causal diamonds for a specious present; Stein 1968 fn 6 on proper time)
assumptions: Secondary exposition of Stein's formalization; conditions on R attributed to Stein 1968: reflexive, transitive (as SEP presents them), non-universal; the fully precise original conditions (including the hereditary condition and symmetry option) are in Stein 1968, which this lane could not access.
conclusion: Per SEP: Stein showed there is a unique non-universal two-place 'becoming' relation definable from Minkowski structure (the past causal cone of each event), which blocks the Rietdijk-Putnam-Penrose argument IF the definition is accepted; the cost is that becoming becomes event-relative and the present degenerates to a single event; Callender objects that this is too thin. SEP also warns (Sec. 3.2, citing Sellars discussion) that adopting the spacetime framework is not tantamount to eternalism.
proof_status: Secondary exposition; Stein 1968 remains unread (all public routes blocked, see AGENT_REPORT).
open_questions: Obtain Stein 1968 full text (JSTOR/PDC paywalled) to audit the exact theorem statement and its conditions before any formal use.
relevance: Connects the definability line to the becoming/open-future line; the Stein uniqueness result is the becoming-side analog of Malament's uniqueness, and shares the same logical status (a definability theorem given chosen constraints).
limits: Secondary; explicitly not a substitute for the primary theorem statement.
